It is also, inevitably, a hotbed of crime, corporate espionage and political intrigue.

regions.name: Orion
regions.notable_for: Five-world system; home of the Galactic Union; birthplace of OrionWorks
regions.desc: The Orion system is the political and corporate centre of the known galaxy, five worlds across every stage of construction, ruin, and ambition. Home to the Galactic Union and the ghost of OrionWorks, the organisation that built artificial planets and may have started the Tronik War. It is heavily defended, intensely surveilled, and the kind of place where what you know and who you know matters more than what you can do.

regions.name: Aderan
regions.notable_for: Galaxy's largest for-profit prison; home of Ridge Racing, Survivor and Blood Bowl
regions.desc: The Aderan system was the site of the first corporate war in galactic history, a conflict that ended with Aderan Prime destroyed and everyone finally understanding that there was no upper limit to what corporate warfare could do. The surviving world, Aderan 3, found a highly profitable replacement economy: the galaxy's largest for-profit prison, and the broadcast rights to three of its most watched shows.

regions.name: Mangara
regions.faction: Contested, Hakari clans vs Jaulaus tribes
regions.notable_for: Homeworld of Hakari and Jaulaus; continuous civil war; Alliance embargo
regions.desc: Mangara is the homeworld of the Hakari and Jaulaus and one of the most uncomfortable chapters in Alliance history. Exploited by the Nerulian Empire and then by corporate interests, placed under Alliance embargo to protect what remains of its traditional life, and still burning from an inter-species civil war that has never stopped. Protected on paper, exploited in practice, ignored in fact.

regions.name: Carach System
regions.notable_for: Skalan homeworld Caragh; sacred ground of a species that survived an attempted extinction
regions.desc: The Carach system is the heart of Skalan civilisation. Caragh, the homeworld, is closed to non-Skalans without exception or negotiation. The system is self-governed under a Warrior Council elected by combat reputation. Skalan patrol vessels enforce the system perimeter without legal frameworks or diplomatic language.

regions.name: Seigh System
regions.notable_for: Most lethal natural environment in the known galaxy; Skalan rite of passage
regions.desc: Seigh is a separate system from Carach, administered by the Skalan as a closed training world. Every survey that has assessed the planet reaches the same conclusion: it is the most lethal naturally occurring environment in the known galaxy. Non-Skalans are not welcome. The fauna does not check jurisdiction before acting.

regions.name: Berilia
regions.notable_for: Patriark homeworld; most advanced cloning facilities in the galaxy
regions.desc: Berilia is the Patriark homeworld and the quiet centre of the galaxy's most important dependency: resurrection technology. The Patriarks built no army. Instead they spent centuries making themselves indispensable. The cloning infrastructure on Berilia underpins the Alliance's promise of continuity, and the Patriarks know exactly what it would cost everyone if they renegotiated their terms.

regions.name: Ishtar
regions.notable_for: Arms Corp HQ; largest manufacturing world in the galaxy; volcanic terrain; toxic atmosphere
regions.desc:
Ishtar exists to produce. The volcanic geology provides near-limitless geothermal energy. The crust is mineral-dense enough that raw materials are extracted metres from where they are processed. The atmosphere is permanently toxic from centuries of unregulated industrial output, workers wear breathers outside sealed zones.

The weapons that come out of Ishtar's foundries are carried by soldiers on every side of every war in the galaxy.

regions.name: Damph
regions.notable_for: Only known source of Coronthia in the galaxy; frozen surface; intense blue-collar worker culture
regions.desc:
Damph is a frozen hellhole that happens to sit on the only known deposits of Coronthia in the galaxy, a super-dense fuel compound of extraordinary power and extraordinary instability.

The workers who extract it know exactly how much leverage that gives them. Governed by a patchwork of worker clans, tough, territorial, deeply suspicious of outsiders, and fiercely proud of what they do. Corporate interests are present but operate carefully.

regions.name: Alsa
regions.notable_for: Most fertile worlds in the galaxy; primary food source for Alliance Space
regions.desc: Alsa is where the galaxy eats. The system's worlds are extraordinarily fertile, geology, climate and water distribution aligned in a combination that produces agricultural output unmatched anywhere in known space. Most of the food consumed across Alliance Space originates here in some form. Alsa is quiet, green, and largely pastoral, and the most heavily insured system in the Alliance, protected by standing navy contracts that make attacking it extremely inadvisable.

regions.name: Ash
regions.notable_for: Gateway to the Nemani Rift; military staging point; salvage culture; glory-seekers and rift pilots
regions.desc: Ash would be an unremarkable frontier system if it were not sitting at the edge of the Nemani Rift. The Alliance military maintains a permanent and substantial presence here, monitoring the Rift and ensuring that whatever is on the other side stays on the other side. Around the military has grown an ecosystem of salvage yards, scrappers, black market dealers, and pilots who come here specifically to attempt the Rift. Most of those pilots do not come back. The ones who do come back wealthy, famous, or permanently changed.

regions.name: Palentium
regions.notable_for: First human-discovered planet in Alliance Space; tropical climate; luxury tourism; pervasive corruption
regions.desc: Palentium was the first planet humans set foot on in what is now Alliance Space, a fact the tourism industry has milked for centuries. The world is genuinely beautiful: tropical, warm, blessed with long coastlines and an atmosphere that requires no modification. The corruption is so deeply embedded into Palentium's institutions that most residents treat it as a natural feature of the climate. Everything is for sale on Palentium if you know who to ask.
